verdicts.evidence: A hole of minimal reach, stated as such — and in the direction of a behaviour MORE correct than the shipped one. Divergence measured by direct function call: mission at the 127th ancestor of the cwd → identical; at exactly the 128th ancestor → shipped null, mutated finds the root. On the real CLI (a chain of 128 directories built under tmp, path of 675 bytes, under PATH_MAX): shipped exit 2 "No runward/ mission found here or above. Run `runward init` first." — a FALSE sentence, the mission exists above, exactly the lie that raising the cap from 12 to 128 had corrected —; mutated exit 1 with the mission's real audit. Nothing sees it: mission.test.js pins the climb at depth 3 and 20 and the orphan at null, nothing at 128; the header of mission-boundaries.test.js declares both bounds of the climb "deliberately not pinned" (freezing them would freeze an arbitrary bound) — a documented choice, but under ADR-0046 the mutant changes an exit code on a constructible input that nothing holds: hole, perimeter = nesting of exactly 128 under the mission root. Full replay of the net on the mutant: all green.

verdicts.evidence: Same family as the bound mutant, in a "cap removed" version. i-- makes the condition i<128 always true but NEVER creates an infinite loop: the root break holds (dirname is purely lexical and reaches its fixed point "/" in fewer iterations than the path's depth — measured: orphan → null, normal termination). The only effect is the disappearance of the 128 ceiling: divergence measured by direct function call with a mission at the 130th ancestor (shipped null, mutated finds it) and on the real CLI from a chain of 130 directories (path of 685 bytes): shipped exit 2 "No runward/ mission found here or above" (false), mutated exit 1 with the real audit. Nothing sees it: no fixture of the net goes beyond depth 20, and mission-boundaries.test.js documents the deliberate non-pinning of the climb's bounds. A hole of minimal reach (nesting >127), full replay of the net on the mutant green. The code comment itself says that the bound guards a "pathological symlink cycle" that cannot exist (dirname never touches the filesystem): the mutant survives because the bound guards nothing reachable.

verdicts.evidence: REALISTIC hole: the mission marker becomes "a runward/ directory exists" (join(dir,"runward","") = dir/runward) instead of "runward/framing.md exists" — precisely the distinction the code comment claims ("a directory merely named runward … does not count"). Two recipes measured on the real CLI. (1) Directory with runward/ without framing.md (hand-made scaffold, amputated mission), nothing above: shipped exit 2 "No runward/ mission found"; mutated exit 1 while AUDITING this non-mission ("✗ Framing note — file missing") — verdict and remediation changed. (2) The wrong tree judged: a GREEN mission (the example, also replayed as a git repository) containing a half-scaffolded vendor/tool/runward/ without framing; `check` from vendor/tool: shipped exit 0 judging the outer mission (the mission field of check --json = the green root); mutated exit 1 judging vendor/tool — the gate turns red on the WRONG tree, and the mission field of the machine contract names the wrong tree. Nothing sees it: every fixture of the net creates runward/ WITH framing.md (unit, smoke, example, repository), so both forms coincide there; full replay of the net on the mutant green (7 legs + self-gate exit 0).

verdicts.evidence: Equivalent, argued and measured. The root break becomes unreachable, but the capped loop returns the same result on every input: dirname is a pure, monotonic lexical function — every absolute path converges to "/" (or a drive root) and STAYS there, every relative one to "." — and the existence test precedes the break, so even a mission at the filesystem root is found by both forms on the same loop turn, BEFORE the break counts. After the fixed point, the mutant only re-tests the same directory (same argument to existsSync → same answer within one run) until i=128 is exhausted, then returns null like the shipped build. Sensitivity control: a divergence would require either a dirname that is not idempotent at its fixed point (impossible: a lexical function, no filesystem access, so no symlink cycle affects it), or a mutation of the filesystem DURING the loop (a concurrent write race, not an input). Measured identical: direct function call on a deep orphan (128 levels), on "/", on a nested mission, on a simple orphan; real CLI: exit 2/2, identical messages. Only cost: ~120 superfluous existsSync calls after the root — invisible. This is one of the "two bounds of the root climb" that mission-boundaries.test.js declares equivalent and deliberately unpinned; here the equivalence is real, not merely decreed.
